title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Daughter
review: Mara Ellison is luminous as the keeper's daughter. The slow pacing pays off in a final act that left me in tears.

title: Neon Harbor
review: A noisy, empty thriller. The car chases are loud and the plot makes no sense after the first twenty minutes.

title: Paper Kingdoms
review: Director Tomas Reyes builds a gentle fable about two brothers who run a print shop. Charming, if a little too long.

title: Gravity of Small Things
review: I laughed from start to finish. Jonah Pike's deadpan delivery steals every scene he is in.

title: Saltwater Hymns
review: Beautiful cinematography, but the story about a fishing village losing its harbor never finds its emotional center.

title: The Last Train to Oriel
review: A tense mystery on a night train. The twist is clever and Mara Ellison plays the conductor with quiet menace.

title: Copper Sky
review: Boring. Two hours of people staring at the desert while the soundtrack does all the work.

title: Little Engines
review: An animated delight about a family of robots who adopt a stray cat. Kids and adults will both love it.

title: Midnight Ledger
review: The accounting-fraud plot is surprisingly gripping, and Tomas Reyes directs with a sure hand.

title: Wild Orchard
review: Forgettable romance. The leads have no chemistry and the dialogue is painfully stiff.

title: Echoes Under Ice
review: A documentary about Antarctic research stations. Informative and calm, though it rarely surprises.

title: The Borrowed Summer
review: A warm coming-of-age story. Iris Calder gives a heartfelt performance as the grandmother who teaches everyone to sail.

title: Static Bloom
review: Experimental and frustrating. I admire the ambition but could not follow what was happening.

title: Ferryman's Wager
review: A clever heist comedy with sharp writing. Jonah Pike and Iris Calder are a fantastic double act.

title: Glass Meridian
review: Gorgeous science fiction about a city that floats above the clouds. The ending is abrupt but the world-building is superb.

title: Quiet Orbit
review: An astronaut stranded alone talks to her ship's computer. Tense, moving and beautifully acted.

title: Tinder and Rust
review: Overlong war drama. The battle scenes are impressive but the characters are thin.

title: The Pickle Jar Society
review: A silly comedy about competitive pickling that somehow works. I have not laughed this hard in years.

title: Northbound Static
review: The plot about a radio host receiving messages from the future is great, but the third act falls apart.

title: Harbor Lights
review: A sweet, small film. Tomas Reyes clearly loves these characters and so did I.

title: The Orchard Thief
review: Predictable crime drama. You can guess the ending from the poster.

title: Paper Moons
review: Visually inventive animation with a moving story about grief. Mara Ellison voices the moon with real tenderness.

title: Second Shift
review: A realistic portrait of night-shift nurses. Hard to watch at times, but important.

title: The Velvet Detour
review: Style over substance. Every shot looks like a perfume ad and nothing happens.

title: Lantern Season
review: A festival romance with genuine charm. The lantern sequences are breathtaking.

title: Iron Meadow
review: A muddled fantasy epic. Too many characters, too many subplots, too little heart.

title: Small Hours
review: Iris Calder anchors this quiet drama about an insomniac radio host with a career-best performance.

title: Crosswind
review: Fun aviation adventure with great flying sequences, even if the romance subplot drags.

title: The Ninth Recipe
review: A cozy kitchen mystery. Jonah Pike plays the bumbling chef-detective to perfection.

title: Ashfall
review: Relentlessly grim disaster movie. Technically accomplished but exhausting to sit through.
